title: Detector trial
description: One line of a detection ledger (<venture>/governance/detectors/<id>.trials.jsonl). A trial line is one call: the score, the criterion in force and the call. A resolution line comes later, names the trial and says how it turned out: hit, miss, false alarm or correct rejection. The file is append-only: each line carries the hash of the line before, as the provenance log does, so an edited or deleted line breaks the chain. Silence is no data: a trial with no resolution is unresolved. Design: docs/design/SIGNAL_DETECTION_2026-11-07.md.

kind.description: trial: a call was made. resolution: a call was settled.

id.description: The line's id, unique in the file.

detector.description: The id of the detector the line belongs to.

at.description: When the call was made or settled.

criterion.description: trial only: the criterion in force when the call was made, copied from the detector: its lines as numbers, or route person.

call.description: trial only: the call. unsure: the score fell between the two lines and went to a person. Under route person, the call is the person's.

provenance.description: trial only: the hash of the provenance.jsonl line of the write the call judged, when it judged a write.

trial.description: resolution only: the id of the trial it settles.

outcome.description: resolution only: hit, yes and right. miss, no and wrong. false-alarm, yes and wrong. correct-rejection, no and right.

signal.description: resolution only: the signal from operating-rules.json that settled it, when one did.

by.description: resolution only: who settled it, as the detector's resolver names.

id.description: The person, the record that settled it (a venture-relative path), or the producer.

prev.description: The previous line's hash, or genesis for the first line.

hash.description: sha256 of prev followed by this line without its hash field, as JSON with sorted keys.
